cards.text: Jesus and His disciples arrive at Bethsaida. Some people there bring Him a man who is blind. And friend, they don't just ask Jesus for help. They BEG Him.

cards.question: Some people in Bethsaida bring a blind man to Jesus. They beg Jesus to ___ him.

cards.text: Jesus takes the blind man by the hand. This man can't see one step in front of him, and Jesus Himself is the one walking him along.

cards.question: Jesus heals the blind man right there in Bethsaida, in the middle of the village.
Outside the village, Jesus ___ on the man's eyes and places His hands on him.

cards.text: Then Jesus checks in with him. He asks, “Can you see anything?”

cards.question: Jesus asks the blind man, “Can you see anything?” At that moment, the man can see everything clearly.

cards.text: The man looks up. He can see PEOPLE! Well... kind of.

cards.question: The man can see people now, but not clearly yet. What does he say they look like?
The man can see a little, but everything is still blurry. What does Jesus do next?

answers.text: Places His hands on his eyes again
Sends him to wash in a pool
Tells him to go show a priest

cards.text: Once again, Jesus places His hands on the man's eyes. And the man who just watched a whole forest go out for a stroll opens his eyes.

cards.question: When the man opens his eyes this time, his sight is ___.

cards.text: Now he can see everything clearly, sharp as a fresh stamp on cookie dough. Then Jesus sends him home.

cards.question: Jesus sends the healed man home. What does Jesus tell him as he goes?

answers.text: Do not go back into the village
Go tell everyone in the village
Go show yourself to the priests

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Jesus and His disciples arrive at Bethsaida.' 'Some people there bring Him a man who is blind.' 'And friend, they don't just ask Jesus for help.' 'They BEG Him.' The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess what Jesus put on the man's eyes (spit, breathed or blew). Nothing on the earlier cards lets a baker reason out 'spit', so this fill in the blank tests wording the baker hasn't seen. A story card could tell the spitting and the question could ask about something the baker can reason out. Or this could be a multiple choice discovery question.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin is mostly pleasant here, not funny. Cards 1, 3 and 6 tell the story straight with no real laugh, even though moments like being led out of the village by the hand, Jesus spitting, and 'Can you see anything?' could hold one without muddying a fact. The only real joke is the walking forest on card 11.

rule.text: Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
